meta.title: Improve list rev_fold performance
meta.body_summary: Avoid array allocation in list rev_fold by replacing it with direct recursion, and implement rev_foldi without list reversal.

perf_labels.notes: OpenAI_Codex rewrote rev_fold/rev_foldi without tail recursion; reviewer hackwaly disputed performance claim and no benchmark was provided, leading to closure.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 29 changed lines in a single file, this is a tiny edit by absolute volume. It is a typical small-step performance PR that was closed—not merged—because the reviewer doubted the performance improvement and no benchmark evidence was supplied.

review_details.concern_detail: Reviewer hackwaly noted that the new implementation is not tail recursive and expressed doubt that it would improve performance; no benchmark or profiling data was provided.
review_details.performance_claim: Avoid array allocation and use direct recursion to improve rev_fold/rev_foldi performance.
review_details.antipattern_addressed: array_allocation_in_list_fold (prior behavior; not in taxonomy enum)
review_details.rejection_signals: Maintainer bobzhang closed the PR approximately two days after reviewer flagged the non-tail-recursive implementation, with no follow-up fix.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: The agent produced a non-tail-recursive fold but did not consider stack depth implications for large lists, requiring reviewer intervention to identify the potential performance pitfall.

detection_detail.code_reading: hackwaly read the diff and pointed out that the recursion is not tail-recursive, questioning whether the change would actually improve performance.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: PR body contains no benchmark numbers, profiler references, or reproducible performance measurements; only a narrative description of the change.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No fix was attempted after the comment; the PR was closed by the author without further iteration.

core_change_summary.description: In list/list.mbt, replaced array-based rev_fold with a direct non-tail-recursive helper function go, and implemented rev_foldi via recursion without reversing the list. Minor formatting via moon fmt.
change_trajectory: Single commit: rewrote rev_fold and rev_foldi to eliminate array allocation with direct recursion.

review_signals.summary: Pointed out that the new implementation is not tail recursive and expressed doubt about performance improvement.
Formal review COMMENTED with no body text; substantive feedback delivered in inline comment.
Bot review praised the removal of array allocation and list reversal as performance improvements.
Coveralls reported 100% coverage on changed lines and a slight overall coverage increase.

collaboration_trajectory: Reviewer hackwaly left an inline comment questioning tail recursion and performance about three hours after PR creation.
PR remained unchanged and was closed by author two days later, likely due to the unresolved concern.
